name: How Long Does Concrete Driveway Installation Take?

mainEntity.name: How long does a new concrete driveway take to install in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: How long does a new concrete driveway take to install in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: A new concrete driveway is usually more than a one-day pour. The job typically includes demolition of the old surface if needed, subgrade preparation, base compaction, formwork, reinforcement, concrete placement, finishing, and curing time before vehicles can drive on it. If the site has drainage problems, slope corrections, or permit-related inspections, the project can take longer. In Los Angeles County, weather is usually favorable, but scheduling can still be affected by contractor availability, material delivery, and municipal inspection timing. Homeowners should ask not just how long the pour takes, but how long until the driveway is usable for walking and for parking. They should also confirm whether the contractor will stage the work to minimize blocked access to the garage or street. A clear schedule should include start date, demo day, pour day, cure time, and any required follow-up visits for sealing or touch-ups.
acceptedAnswer.description: A new concrete driveway often takes several days to complete, but the full timeline depends on demolition, grading, base preparation, forming, pouring, curing, and weather. Light foot traffic may be allowed sooner than vehicle traffic. If drainage corrections or permit inspections are needed, the project can take longer than the concrete placement itself.
